newsitem.title: INDIA: India unveils steps to help gold jewellery exports.
newsitem.headline: India unveils steps to help gold jewellery exports.

text.p: India's Commerce Ministry, in a bid to boost jewellery exports, on Monday increased the number of agencies permitted to sell gold and allowed export units to sell a part of their output domestically after paying duty.
"To promote export of gold jewellery, it is proposed to increase the number of nominated agencies permitted to stock gold," the ministry said in its new five-year trade policy for 1997-2002.

Only four state-owned firms, the Minerals and Metals Trading Corp, the State Trading Corp, the State Bank of India and the Handicrafts and Handlooms Export Corp are currently permitted to sell gold to jewellery exporters.
"RBI (Reserve Bank of India) will decide the agencies which will be permitted to import gold and give it to exporters," Commerce Secretary P.P. Prabhu told reporters.
He said the RBI would take all factors into consideration before deciding on the agencies but did not specify the factors.
The ministry statement said with the new steps an adequate quantity of gold would be available to exporters which they could take on a replenishment basis or on outright purchase basis.

"Export-oriented units/export processing zones units in the gem and jewellery sector will be permitted to sell 10 percent of their output in the domestic tariff area on payment of duty," the statement said.
The ministry said under the gem and jewellery replenishment (REP) scheme, third-party exports have been allowed.
With this small exporters would be able to sell their products in the world market and claim REP licences based on a disclaimer certificate from the third party.

The ministry said the facility of a bulk licence for the import of rough diamonds has been liberalised to enable the licence holder to import from any source and not necessarily from London's Diamond Trading Corporation as at present.
The bulk licence holder will also be allowed to export rough diamonds upto 10 percent of the value of rough diamonds imported against the bulk licence.
